summary: Reuses the one existing editor controller and the unchanged ownerOf deepest-root rule, and adds one derived partition of the editor's open tabs into per-workspace strips plus an unowned global strip, so a single tab can only ever appear in one strip. App keeps a session-only selected-tab value per workspace that may be a terminal, a Console or an editor tab; opening a file owned by a workspace switches to that workspace and selects its editor tab in the workspace strip without leaving the workspace view, while a file owned by no workspace still opens the header's global editor view (now a plain, ungrouped strip). A new pane-less EditorSurface (lazy CodeSurface plus the per-tab Save/Save as/Raw/Preview actions and the language/EOL/encoding status bar) is rendered both in the workspace main area and by the global view. Terminals stay mounted and are hidden while an editor tab is shown; the workspace editor surface stays mounted and hidden while a terminal tab is shown, so neither is restarted. ownerOf, the editor core (path dedupe, snapshot, close/bin, 5 MB cap), ZestTabs and the existing explorer-to-editor bridge are reused unchanged; there is no Rust, command, permission, CSP or dependency change. Scale and cost: useEditor memoises its tabs array and App partitions it once per tabs/apps change with O(open tabs x workspaces) work, with no polling, no extra IO and no work at startup; only the visible editor's text is loaded by the existing loader, the strip already scrolls horizontally, and nothing new is read from disk.

additions.title: Keep a workspace editor and its terminals mounted while the other is shown
additions.why: Switching between a file tab and a terminal tab must not restart a terminal or throw away the file's cursor and undo history.
acceptance: Switching from a file tab to a terminal tab and back leaves the terminal running and the file's cursor and undo history intact.
Showing a file tab does not stop, reset or remount any of the workspace's terminals.

additions.title: Keep the global view's selection on an unowned file
additions.why: The global strip must never show a workspace-owned file merely because it was the last editor tab selected.
acceptance: Entering the global editor view with unowned tabs open selects an unowned tab, never a workspace-owned one.
Closing an unowned tab in the global view selects the next unowned tab, or shows the empty state when none remain.
